summary: After approximately three years of private dawah, Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to openly proclaim Islam to his wider clan and then to all of Makkah, leading to the first open confrontations with the Quraysh leadership who began persecuting the new Muslim community.
narrative:
The divine command for open preaching came through two successive revelations. First: 'And warn your nearest kindred' (Quran 26:214), followed by: 'So proclaim openly that which you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists' (Quran 15:94). These verses marked the transition from the private phase of dawah to the public one.

In response to the first command, the Prophet ﷺ gathered the Banu Hashim and the wider Banu Abd al-Muttalib at a meal — an event recorded in detail by al-Tabari in his Tarikh, drawing from Ibn Ishaq. He called them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that he is the Messenger of Allah, and asked who among them would be his helper and brother in this matter. Only Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), who was then a young boy, stood up and affirmed his support. The Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on Ali's neck and announced him as his brother in this matter — a statement that became one of the most discussed passages in early Islamic historiography, with scholars such as Ibn Kathir carefully noting its context and scope.

The second and broader public announcement took place at the hill of al-Safa. Ibn Hisham records that the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Safa and called out using the traditional warning cry: 'Ya sabahah!' — the alarm call used when danger approached. The Quraysh gathered, curious. He then called each clan of the Quraysh by name and said: 'If I told you that behind this mountain there is an enemy cavalry about to attack you, would you believe me?' They said: 'We have never known you to lie.' He said: 'Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' His uncle Abu Lahab responded with contempt: 'Tabban laka! Is this why you gathered us?' — and walked away. Surah al-Masad (111) was subsequently revealed condemning Abu Lahab and his wife.

The open call brought immediate and fierce opposition from the Quraysh leadership, who recognized the threat Islam posed to their social order, their control over the Kaabah, and their economic interests as custodians of the shrine. The persecutions began: weaker Muslims without tribal protection were subjected to torture. Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) was laid on the burning sand under the desert sun with a heavy rock on his chest; his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf tried to break his resolve, but Bilal repeated 'Ahad, Ahad' — 'One, One' — in affirmation of Allah's oneness. Abu Bakr (RA) purchased Bilal's freedom.

Ammar ibn Yasir (RA), his father Yasir, and his mother Sumayyah (RA) were all subjected to torture. Sumayyah (RA) was killed by Abu Jahl — she became the first martyr in Islam. When the Prophet ﷺ passed by the family of Yasir while they were being tortured, he said: 'Have patience, O family of Yasir. Your promised place is Paradise.' (Recorded by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak and Ibn Hisham.)

The public phase also saw the famous conversion of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA) — both major figures whose acceptance of Islam significantly strengthened the community. Umar's conversion, occurring after a dramatic sequence of events including an encounter with his sister Fatimah and her husband who were secretly reciting Surah Ta-Ha, is recorded with vivid detail by Ibn Hisham. Ibn Kathir notes that after Umar and Hamzah accepted Islam, the Muslims prayed openly in the Masjid al-Haram for the first time.
